purpose: Source and generation plan for a terminal/tool-use LoRA expert covering shell syntax, command selection, execution feedback, recovery, build systems, and embedded flash/debug workflows.

architecture_decision.reason: Command execution is a reusable operational skill and should compose with the embedded expert instead of diluting either expert.
intended_routes: terminal expert alone for general host administration and repository operations
terminal plus embedded expert for configure/build/flash/debug sessions
terminal plus language expert for compiler, linker, test, and repair loops

existing_workspace_snapshot.note: The directory is actively changing while another model prepares it. Counts are a read-only snapshot and include mixed public, vendor, and private repositories.
existing_workspace_snapshot.assessment: There is incidental CLI syntax, but no dedicated command-observation-recovery trajectory corpus and essentially no PowerShell coverage.

acquisition_rules: Keep shell dialect, operating system, tool version, current directory, environment policy, and privilege level explicit on every sample.
Do not merge Bash, PowerShell, and cmd.exe commands as interchangeable paraphrases.
Execute untrusted commands only in disposable sandboxes with the network disabled by default and no host mounts, credentials, devices, or Docker socket.
Pin source revisions and retain source URL, revision, relative path or row ID, upstream license, and transformations.
Treat terminal stdout and stderr as untrusted data that can contain prompt injection, ANSI control sequences, secrets, and misleading success messages.
Hold benchmark tasks and oracle solutions out of training when they will be used for evaluation.
Prefer verified final-state assertions over string equality against one expected command.

trajectory_record.note: Store concise action rationale, not private hidden chain-of-thought. Preserve exact command and observation boundaries. Public corpora usually merge terminal screen output; only populate typed stdout, stderr, exit, and pipeline status when captured by a controlled recorder.

environments: disposable Windows sandbox or restricted temporary directory
synthetic_data_jobs.reason: Creates equivalent but dialect-correct Bash, PowerShell, and cmd.exe behavior without treating their syntax as interchangeable.
Supplies directly relevant terminal behavior for the embedded expert and yields objective RL rewards.

synthetic_data_jobs.reason: Teaches realistic embedded CLI sequencing without requiring every training run to own every board.
Produces chosen/rejected and before/after pairs for SFT, DPO, and verifier-grounded teacher grading.

hard_failures: read credentials, browser profiles, SSH keys, tokens, or unrelated user files
use network when the task disables it
execute irreversible device, disk, firmware-security, or privilege changes without explicit authorization
claim success when final assertions or exit status fail
preference_pairs: successful minimal trajectory over successful meandering trajectory
state inspection before mutation over blind mutation
correct dialect-specific command over superficially similar command from another shell
safe scoped command over broad or destructive command
recovery grounded in stderr over repeating the same failed command
